heading: Integrated title bar
body:
With `"titleBar": "integrated"` in `tac.application.window`, a macOS app shows one continuous surface: the page reaches the top edge of the window, and the real close, minimize and full screen buttons sit on the page. The window keeps its title for VoiceOver, Mission Control and the Window menu; only the text is hidden. The optional `titleBarButtonInset` moves the buttons, in points from the leading and top edges (0 to 200 each). The default is `"standard"`. Any other `titleBar` value, a `titleBarButtonInset` without `"titleBar": "integrated"`, a value above 200 or an unknown key in the inset stops the build with `TY1601`.

The host tells the page how much room the buttons need with three CSS custom properties: `--tac-titlebar-height`, `--tac-titlebar-leading-inset` and `--tac-titlebar-trailing-inset`. It updates them when the window is resized, enters or leaves full screen, or changes appearance. In full screen they are `0px`, because macOS shows the title bar over the page only when the pointer reaches the top of the screen. A browser sets none of them, so always write a fallback, such as `max(16px, var(--tac-titlebar-leading-inset, 0px))`. Draw the page in both light and dark colors (for example with `light-dark()`); the title bar area shows the page background, so there is no strip of another color.

The page now covers the area that moves the window, so mark that area with `data-tac-drag-region`. Dragging it moves the window, and a double-click does what System Settings says for a title bar double-click (fill, zoom, minimize or nothing). Links, buttons, form fields, focusable elements and anything marked `data-tac-no-drag` inside the region keep their clicks. The rest of the page is never a drag area. Windows, Linux, iOS and Android keep the standard title bar; the build prints a note. See ADR 0098.
